worldcombat.skill.earthpower.summary: Make the real support surface under the target erupt from below: it hits only foes on the same support surface whose feet lie inside the mark, dealing special damage and launching them up, and may lower their Sp. Def by 1 stage. Airborne targets pass above the surge.
worldcombat.skill.earthpower.use.0: Strike a grounded target from range through its feet
worldcombat.skill.earthpower.use.1: Launch a point-blank foe off the ground
worldcombat.skill.earthpower.use.2: Skip fliers and drifters, punish planted foes
worldcombat.skill.earthpower.use.3: Foes on a different floor than the mark are spared
worldcombat.skill.earthpower.description: The erupting ground deals about %1$s special damage.
Every grounded foe within %1$s blocks of the target's feet on the same support surface is caught and launched upward at %2$s blocks per tick.
Each foe caught has a %1$s chance to have its Sp. Def lowered by %2$s stage(s); every stage of lower Sp. Def means it takes more special damage.
Wind-up %1$s (the foe's window to step away), range %2$s blocks; the surge erupts upward at the mark, with clods and column height driven by the real mechanic values.
worldcombat.skill.earthpower.timing: Range %1$s blocks, wind-up %2$s, recovery %3$s, %4$s PP, cooldown %5$s.
worldcombat.skill.earthpower.growth.0: From level %1$s the surge rises to %2$s power and %3$s blocks of range.
On: burst radius ×1.4 and clods ×1.3, but power ×0.88 and +4 ticks cooldown — covers a small patch around the target's feet. Off: a narrower, harder single column for naming one target.
Beyond this distance the companion closes in first. Larger values let it raise the ground under more distant targets.
On: slow-moving targets rank higher, since the surge rises at their feet and a still target is least likely to step out while the mark shows. Off: every target ranks the same.
worldcombat.skill.earthpower.description: With fissure form on, the burst radius and clods are larger but the column is a little weaker with a longer cooldown, covering a small patch at the target's feet; with it off, the column is narrower and harder, for naming a single target.
